headline: TWO supertankers carrying 4.5M barrels combined struck naval mines on 'unauthorized southern route' in the Strait of Hormuz
dek: IRGC Navy: two supertankers on an 'unauthorized' southern route in the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines; engine rooms disabled by explosions and intense fires; both vessels immobilized and abandoned by crews near the southern coast. Combined cargo >4.5 million barrels of crude.

sections.what_happened: IRGC Navy: two supertankers on an 'unauthorized' southern route in the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines; engine rooms disabled by explosions and intense fires; both vessels immobilized and abandoned by crews near the southern coast. Combined cargo >4.5 million barrels of crude. IRGC released footage of the strikes on state TV. Separately (Thursday, via IRIB): 4 ships transferring oil in the northern Persian Gulf were 'hit simultaneously and caught fire' after crossing 'illegal routes'; 3 other vessels struck mines in the western Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday night. Iranian state TV: seven tankers damaged overnight. IRGC warns US bases across the region will be targeted if Washington keeps assisting transits.
sections.what_verified: Claim-reported by 2+ declared-tier families: Iranian state media (IRGC/IRNA/Mehr/Press TV, T3 STATE(IR)) as originator; Anadolu Agency (T3 STATE(TR)) via anews.com.tr and AA-derived Turkish outlets. Al Mayadeen (footage), Business Standard, Turkiye Today carry with attribution but have NO declared tier and do not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: US disputes Iran's mine claims (Al Mayadeen note; Trump on Truth Social accused Tehran of fabricating claims to inflate crude prices ahead of the Nov 3 midterms). AP (seen via secondary quoting only — direct AP piece not yet located): October had the highest number of reported attacks on commercial shipping since March; some shipping companies have become less willing to report incidents — i.e. the open record may UNDERCOUNT. UKMTO had not reported the latest attacks (LinkedIn/AP-quote). PortWatch (independent, T1): counted only 4 transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18, 7-day avg 3.71 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day (4.3% of baseline) — consistent with the strait being effectively shut, but says nothing about the mine claims themselves.
sections.why_matters: While Washington talks 'freedom of navigation,' Tehran is the one physically controlling the waterway — and it just released the footage. The counted numbers say the strait is running at 4% of normal traffic. Two claimed mine strikes, 4.5 million barrels, crews abandoning ship — reported as Iran's claim, with the US denial on the record.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE (big-missed; IRGC statement Friday Oct 23) -- IRGC Navy: TWO supertankers carrying 4.5M barrels combined struck naval mines on 'unauthorized southern route' in the Strait of Hormuz, engines disabled, crews abandoned; IRGC releases footage. Thursday IRIB claim: 4 oil ships hit simultaneously in northern Gulf + 3 struck mines west of Hormuz (7 tankers damaged per Iranian state TV).

totw_analysis: Our read: While Washington talks 'freedom of navigation,' Tehran is the one physically controlling the waterway — and it just released the footage. The counted numbers say the strait is running at 4% of normal traffic. Two claimed mine strikes, 4.5 million barrels, crews abandoning ship — reported as Iran's claim, with the US denial on the record. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Iran enforcing legitimate maritime control as a coastal state (Baghaei: 'legitimate, legal') or holding the world's oil hostage — and are the mine strikes real, or fabricated to spike prices before the US midterms, as Trump claims?
